newsitem.title: CANADA: Gulf says has no immediate Arctic plans.
newsitem.headline: Gulf says has no immediate Arctic plans.

text.p: Gulf Canada Resources Ltd has no immediate plans to mount an oil drilling program in Canada's high Arctic, a company spokesman said on Tuesday.

The government of Canada said earlier it granted two new exploration licences in the Mackenzie Delta region of the Northwest Territories to Gulf Canada and Husky Oil Ltd entitling each firm to drill one well during the nine-year life of each permit.
"The driver behind this was the land settlement, not the Husky and Gulf needs," said Gulf's John Sparks. "We just agreed in order to expedite that whole process to do this trade now."

The licences were granted in exchange for 21 former permits for the Cape Bathurst area, east of the Mackenzie Delta. The region was part of land given back to the native Inuvialuit people as part of a 1984 settlement.
"It's essentially us agreeing that in order for the settlement to be completed, we'd make the exchange," Sparks said.
